utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in the courtroom and to those listening and visiting the proceedings here in the courtroom. As you can see, there are only two Judges present. Judge Nyambe is not with us at the moment. For reasons I can't tell you at the moment, but especially because of the videolink which was established, the remaining Judges decided to sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis of our Rules of Procedure and evidence. I know we want to discuss some procedural matters today, but we should do that at the end of today's hearing because of the videolink which was set up. There were some technical problems, I was told, and therefore we have a certain delay of our proceeding today. I would kindly ask the Registrar to set up the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. We are -- we have now a connection to another country. We see on our screen here in the courtroom the face of the protected witness who has to testify today, together with a Court Officer sitting next to him. First I would like to know, do you understand me and do you receive a proper interpretation, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Please rise and read aloud the affirmation which is shown to you now by the Court Officer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down and make yourself comfortable. You are informed about the proceedings. You have protection. Your name -- your real name should not be mentioned in these proceedings, and nobody will see your face. First, the Prosecutor, Ms. Hasan, will put questions to you. And after that, the accused, Mr. Tolimir. Ms. Hasan, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: To begin, could we have the pseudonym sheet 65 ter 7520 shown to the witness without being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you will now be shown a piece of paper, and without reading it out loud, could you please confirm that the name that appears underneath PW-014 is your name.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes, it is my name.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would offer 65 ter 7520 into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 7520 shall be assigned Exhibit P2616 under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, I just want to remind you that there will be some questions I will ask you that may reveal your identity. I will only do so in what we call private session. This means that nobody outside of this courtroom will hear what you say. And just a reminder, to me and you, to just speak slowly so the interpreters can interpret what we say. Mr. Witness, have you recently had the opportunity to listen to your testimony that you gave in the Popovic et al. case on the 2nd and 3rd of November, 2006?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Was the evidence that you gave in that trial true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes, it was completely truthful and accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would then offer the admission of his Popovic testimony into evidence. The under seal version has already been MFI'd with number P2237, and the public version of that transcript has 65 ter number 6510.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Both versions will be received, the first one under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 6501 [sic] shall be assigned Exhibit P2237, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask you to check the 65 ter number in the list. I have 65 ter 6509.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For clarification, 65061 -- 6510 had been already assigned P2237. 1 -- 6509.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think you should -- we have many problems on the transcript now. Please check again. I think 65 ter 6509 is that one which was marked for identification, and it will be now received under P2237. The other one is we are 6510 and should be given a P number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 6510 shall be assigned Exhibit P2617. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Hasan, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I then move to offer in -- the exhibits that were admitted through the witness's testimony in Popovic. There are a number on the list that already have -- were already admitted as exhibits in this case, so I offer the remaining documents; namely, 65 ter 1373 and 1374; 65 ter 1020; and 1021; 65 ter 6511 through to 6515; and 65 ter 3343 and 3344.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They will be received and given P numbers by an internal memorandum to save some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I will --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, internal memorandum shall be distributed as soon as the numbers have been assigned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And with your permission, I will now read a summary of the witness's testimony from the Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness PW-014 resided in the Srebrenica municipality in July 1995. He was 16 years old at the time. Around 9 July, the witness, along with his father, mother, and siblings, moved to the centre of Srebrenica town to escape the shelling of his home village. On 11 July 1995, the witness, along with his father and brother, decided to follow the crowd in the direction of Tuzla. His mother and sister left in the direction of Potocari. The witness was situated towards the rear of the column and recalled the shelling and ambushes that took place over the course of 11 and 12 July. He was separated from his father and brother in Buljim. While searching for them, he came across some 50 armed Muslim men and eventually found his father who had been injured during an ambush. He saw other men who had been shot dead. On 13 July, the witness arrived near an asphalt road. From there, he heard calls for them to surrender and saw what appeared to be an UNPROFOR personnel carrier and blue helmets. The soldiers promised safe passage. After receiving two ultimatums, the witness, along with his brother and father, surrendered. The witness was taken to a meadow. There, soldiers asked -- sorry, before reaching the meadow, soldiers asked everyone to hand over money and valuables and to drop their belongings in piles before reaching Sandici meadow where the witness was detained with approximately 1.000 other men. He watched as the Bosnian Serb soldiers took men to a cornfield. Those men did not return. That afternoon, on 13 July, the witness was told to fetch water and distribute it to the other prisoners. He heard cries from a house as he passed by it. A bus carrying women and children arrived at Sandici meadow and stopped near to where the witness was collecting water. The driver of the bus told the witness to get some water for him and put it next to the wheel. While the driver was speaking to some soldiers, the witness got on the bus and hid under some luggage. Early in the morning, the witness reunited with his brother in Dubrava after being transferred there from Kladanj. During his testimony, the witness recalled the identities of various people whom he saw in the column and at Sandici meadow, including his father, whom he saw for the very last time at Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If I may now have P991 played, and this is the Srebrenica trial video.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you were shown some clips from this video, and you have previously identified various locations and individuals depicted in that video. I am going to show you a clip that you have seen before.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And for that, Mr. President, we will have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you see --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the image in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I'd like to ask you about the person who is to the very left of that image. Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, we don't see a picture in front of us. Perhaps we have to go to another channel. I have no idea how to get it. Thank you. We have it now in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, this is an image taken from the video we just saw, and I'd like to ask you about the person to the very left on that image. Do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes, I know that man personally. I know his name and I knew him back in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us his name.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: His name is Almir.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did Almir survive?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: When we came to the house, just after this portion shown in the picture, Almir was told to take off his shirt. And they said to him, Where did you get that shirt, you mother fucker? That's what the soldiers said. And they left Almir at that house. He never came to the meadow. And I know that Almir was buried this year in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 3343 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, this is an image that you were shown during the Popovic trial. Do you recognise the location?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And do you recall making the red markings that are on this image?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Would you then please orient us using what you have already marked on this image and show us or tell us where it was that you collected water from.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Where this house is, looking to the left at the screen, the spot where it says "tank," it's a hundred metres to the left, the place where we drew water.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: When you went to collect water, were you the only person to do so?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No. There were others, I believe four boys of my age who also went collect water.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could revert back to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, at this point in time I would like to ask you: You have used two documents, 65 ter 6512, and 65 ter 3343, are you tendering them?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, they are amongst those that were shown -- admitted through the witness during Popovic, so they are part of the 65 ter numbers I read out earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This clarifies the situation. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention then to, Witness, when you were still in the hills, before you started to hear calls for your surrender. And I'd like to ask you about those calls. Do you recall what you were being told, whether it was over the megaphone or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I remember that they used megaphones.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us what it is that they were telling you.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Well, you know, there were two ultimatums before we came down to surrender. The first time, they said, Surrender, nobody will do anything to you. Resid is here, the former chief from Bratunac. And all that time they were telling us that the blue helmet soldiers from UNPROFOR were there. "Nothing will happen to you." We could see the asphalt road from where we were, and we could see an UN transporter driving by. I knew it very well from Srebrenica. And, yes, we could see blue helmets. Our impression was that what they were saying about UNPROFOR was true. That's why we were sure that UNPROFOR soldiers were there and that there was a chance that we would stay alive, that they would not kill us.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much for testifying once again and for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before Mr. Tolimir commences his cross-examination, Judge Mindua has a question. And after that, we should have an earlier break today. Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness. You said that from the place where you were you could observe a UN vehicle and that you could also see several blue helmets down there. However, when you came down, was it really -- when you surrendered, was that really a UN vehicle? Were they -- were those really UN soldiers, blue helmets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we did see the UN vehicle and the blue helmets on the asphalt road that we could see from the hilltop where we were. As we started walking down to the meadow, we were in a state of shock because our first contact with the Serb soldiers revealed that they were the ones wearing the blue helmets and that they wore UN flak jackets. They were not UNPROFORs. They only used their gear. And the transporter, the Serbs were on the transporter. They were the ones who were using it. I saw some 10 or 15 soldiers who sported the same gear that UNPROFOR wore in Srebrenica. We were in a state of total shock when we came down and when we realised that they were not UNPROFOR soldiers. And then we saw that we -- that was just the bait for us, to lure us down from the forest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should have our first break now. And before we break, I would kindly ask Mr. Tolimir to give us an estimation of the length of his cross-examination. Are you able to give us your estimate?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. May God's peace reign in this courtroom and may His will be done in these proceedings and not necessarily mine. I believe that I will need more than one hour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We must have our first break now, and we will resume 10 minutes before 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: As you can see, the Bench is complete now. We are sitting with three Judges again. Sir, you know now it's the turn of Mr. Tolimir to conduct his cross-examination, and he will put questions to you. Mr. Tolimir, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to greet everybody in the courtroom, including Judge Nyambe, who has just joined us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to greet the witness - I don't want to mention his name - and all those who are in the same place where the witness is. May today's day complete in keeping with God's will, as well as the whole trial. I would like to invite the witness to answer my questions based on what he remembers and knows about the events. Sir, I'm not going to mention your name, but let me tell you that we will talk about your statement. Under tab 1, 06516 is the number of the exhibit. We see the statement and now we will look at the third paragraph in the statement, and I will read from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is under seal and should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We are waiting for 65 ter 6516, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see this document. Sir, could you please tell us whether you remember how was decision reached on leaving Srebrenica and separating men from women, the elderly from the able-bodied men, how was a decision reached to start walking over the mountain towards Tuzla? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: The decision for us to start walking across the woods and for my mother and my sister to go towards Potocari was made exclusively by us. That was a decision made by ourselves. I knew that if I were to go to Potocari that would mean a certain death, and we hoped that if we went across the forest that there was a good chance for us to stay alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us if you made that decision for your family? Who was it who made the decision for all the families in Srebrenica, for women and children to go to Potocari and for the men to go through the wood? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you saying no because you don't want to tell us? Can you explain how come that all the families were unanimous in their decision? Was it just a chance happening, or was there a previous decision made at a higher level?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I can give you my opinion, only. I believe that after everything that happened in the course of 1992 and 1993 and the shelling that happened on the 6th of July, we knew what the Serbian Army wanted to do. They wanted to kill us all. And in my view no smart person would have ever dreamt of heading towards Potocari. My opinion is that everybody decided for themselves to go through the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, that is your opinion that you share with us now. However, at the time, what was the decisive factor for all the families to make that decision? Your father was also a soldier. You said it yourself. Did somebody tell him to impart that decision on his family?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: You know, my father was a soldier just on paper. His name was on records, but he was not an active soldier. He did not have weapons. As I've already told you, he just registered as a member of the BiH Army. And as for the decision, I can't tell you whether some higher force, as it were, or higher command decided that, but everybody was afraid and everybody made their personal decisions or they just followed the majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In that case, could we please look at the third paragraph in your statement, where you say, and I quote: "I was in a group of people that first gathered in the village of Kazani, in the vicinity of Suceska. When we reached Buljim, some officers from the Bosnian army tried to organise the column of several thousands of people with different army units leading them." My question to you is this: In view of the fact that your departure with the military column was organised by army officers, is it possible that army officers conveyed that message to all the families, through soldiers, for family members to go to Potocari and for men and soldiers to go to Susnjari? Is that a likelihood? Is this how things may have transpired?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I believe that we were focussed on Srebrenica and what was happening in Srebrenica in that moment. Susnjari, Buljim, are further away from Srebrenica. When I said this, I meant that there was a subsequent attempt to organise the column, because when we started walking, there was no order among the people. I believe that they tried to organise us in order to provide for a more efficient passage. In Srebrenica itself, my opinion is, and I adhere by that opinion, that nobody tried to organise people where they would go and how they would go. I believe that all those decisions were made individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that in the place where you were lined up there were members of civilian authorities and military authorities from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it possible that they may have reached an agreement to organise a column that would try to break through across Baljkovica to the territory under the control of the BiH Army? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, did officers separate you and tell you what unit to join, or was it up to you to join any unit you wanted?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I really don't know what units those were. I only know that I was moving with a large group of people. I was tired. I fell asleep in the evening on the 11th, and when I woke up on the 12th I was at Buljim. I don't know what had happened in the meantime, whether people were organised into what units. Speaking from my own perspective, neither me nor my people were ever told what to do, where to go. We just followed the crowd.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. However, on the 8th of March, 1999, when you provided this statement, you stated in the third paragraph, in the last sentence or the last two sentences, this is line 7: "A Bosnian army unit, the Mountain Battalion, led by Ejub Golic, had the task to protect this part of the column of civilians. There were about fifty armed soldiers among them [as interpreted]." You were there, and that's why you stated what you stated. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes. I said what I saw at that moment at the place where I was, and I heard that those people who carried those weapons, about fifty of them, that it was their task to protect the rear end of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you observe that they behaved in a military way, and did they protect the flanks of the column? Did you see soldiers on the flanks of the column and at its back?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on to the 5th paragraph in your statement, where you say: "We went down the hill into a creek, 200 to 300 metres down. Here I saw four or five dead bodies dressed in civilian clothes lying on one side of the track. My impression was that they had been hit by bullets to the head and chest area. I had heard firing going on in the area." My question to you is this: Who could have killed those people? Who could have inflicted such injuries on them, only in the head and in the chest? Was that done from close range? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I suppose that it was from close range. But that was the initial shock. That was the horror of the entire situation. Those were the first images of dead people. I was in a state of shock. The first time I smelled blood. And my conclusion was that they were killed from a very close distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let's look at tab 7, and under that tab we will see D270.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, just a question. You have used the OTP statement of the witness. Are you tendering it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to tender the witness's statement into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 6516 shall be assigned Exhibit D319 under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And now let us look at D270. That was provided by a person whose name I am not going to mention because the document is under seal. If we look at the fifth line of the statement, we -- you will see that it reads: "When we left Srebrenica on 11 July 1995, a shell killed five men in a ditch, but I did not know any of them." My question to you is this: You followed the same trail, would you say that those men or those bodies that you saw, is it possible that they were killed by a shell, that they were not killed from a rifle and sustained injuries in the head and in the chest?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't want to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, tell us, did you see the wounds on the bodies by which you were passing, or did you hear the description from somebody else?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I saw them myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In that case, please tell us: Did you follow the same trail that people had walked on previously? They did not belong to your group; they belonged to some other groups. And those dead bodies, did they belong to your group or to some other groups of people who had passed the same way before you?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not know any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you see next to the bodies any eye-witnesses, somebody who had seen how they were killed, somebody who told you that they were killed with bullets hitting them in the head and in the chest?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you say that somebody should have approached the column very close to be able to kill those people by firing in the most sensitive parts of their bodies, in the chest and in the head?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes. It must have been done from a very close range. Maybe they were ambushed or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Would somebody have informed you not to follow the trail to avoid that same ambush?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No. Nobody knew where other people were going. The situation was horrendous. There was shelling, shooting. I don't see how anybody could convey any information to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a while ago, we saw that Golic, the commander of the Mountain Battalion, was in charge of the safety of civilians. You said it yourself in the third passage. Is it possible that he was the one who was supposed to warn you? He was at the rear of the column and he was supposed to protect the civilians. Was it his role to inform you about any problems that you might encounter on the trail that you were to follow?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, let's go to the follow paragraph in your statement, which is paragraph 6. That's tab 1. Let's go back to tab 1, paragraph 6, your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which is now D319.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. Let's look at D319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the sixth paragraph. Now we can see the sixth paragraph, where it says: "I saw seven or eight killed soldiers from the BiH Army, and their throats had been slit." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The trail that you followed, did it pass by the creek where you saw some seven or eight dead Bosnian army soldiers with their throats slit?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yeah, the trail that I followed skirted them, and I could see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you learn from somebody how they had been killed, how the BiH Army soldiers had been killed, or did you make your own inferences?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No, I did not learn the truth. Nobody informed me how they had died. I just saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you remember whether they still had uniforms on which is what made you conclude that they were soldiers? If they did wear uniforms, what kind of uniforms were those? Did they also wear weapons?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Yes, they were in uniforms, which made me conclude that they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And were there weapons on their bodies or next to their bodies? Perhaps grenades, rifles?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: You know, when there are bullets flying above you and when people are running to save their lives, there is hardly time to look at the details and to see who wore what or what was next to the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that their throats had been cut. For somebody to cut their throats, for somebody to slit their throats, would you say that they should have come very close, that they should have touched them, that they should have wrestled them? What would you say?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay, since you don't know, let's go to my next question. But before that: Does that mean that there was fighting along the entire trail that you moved on and that those five or six bodies were the first bodies that you saw? Was there fighting, head-to-head fighting, as it were?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please pause and for the sake of the interpreters so that they can finish their interpretation. Now your next question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, let's look at paragraph 7 in your statement, and I will quote from it. I will read just the penultimate sentence, where you say that: "Some shells fell very close and the shells for fired from hand-held rocket-launchers. I had learned about weapons during high school." My question to you is this: In order for somebody to fire a shell from a hand-held rocket-launcher, does that person have to see the target in order to be able to fire at it?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't see anything strange there. Your soldiers were there and there were moments when we could hear them shouting to each other. They could easily throw grenades on us. They were very close to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since you say you learned about weapons in school, can you tell us the range of a hand-held launcher? Does there have to be visibility for the person holding the launcher?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I am no expert in weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it have been more logical for the shooter to shoot at you from a greater distance than coming close to you to have visibility with a hand-held launcher?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: There was no need. Your soldiers never exposed themselves to any danger, because there was no one armed in that column. If we had been armed, I would have said, Okay, it's legitimate to keep at a greater distance. From where I was, I saw around me only civilians at the time when the Serbian troops were shooting at us. They could choose whether to shoot or to throw grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to go back to anything we've already dealt with, but let me remind you that you were scattered among the units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But why did you state that, then, in the third paragraph of your statement, in the sixth, seventh, eight, and ninth line?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: That is a misinterpretation, a misrepresentation. I said I was towards the tail of the column, which doesn't mean that when we were moving from Buljim along those brooks, across these hillocks, there was anyone armed around me. I didn't see anyone armed around me, nor could I see where the firing was coming from, where your soldiers were. You must be misreading my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I jump in at this point. Sir, I would like to read the specific sentence to you again: "There were about fifty armed soldiers among us." Can you tell us where you have seen these 50 armed soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw them at Buljim, at Buljim. Later on I don't know where they went. I didn't see them in the column again, none of those armed soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you recall that in paragraph 3, line 2, you stated: "When we got to Buljim, some officers of the Bosnian army tried to organise a column of several thousand people led by several army units." Is that again a misreading? That's what you stated.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: That's what I stated, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell the Trial Chamber, was it indeed the case, as you stated it, or was it different?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: That's not the way it was. I emphasize again: I was only following the bulk of the people, and I didn't see again any of those armed units all the way to Sandici. I didn't see anyone firing back. I did not see any organising at all. I'm just telling you what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: But in your statement you said you saw seven to eight dead soldiers of the BH army lying with their throats cut in the low grass. That's what you describe in paragraph 6 of your statement. Were they armed soldiers? Were they soldiers at all?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: They had uniforms on; that's why I called them soldiers. But they had no weapons. We saw them lying in the grass with their throats cut. It was hot. We could smell the blood. That's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let us look at paragraph 9 of your statement, lines 1 through 6. I will read it all out, because we're going to discuss it: "However, suddenly we saw -- we heard a strange noise like a strong gust of wind. We realised we were ambushed, encircled by the Bosnian Serb army. They started shooting from all sides, from hand-held weapons, and they started throwing grenades. We saw many people get killed, but I don't know how many. I decided that we should try to break out of the encirclement and try to get to Kravica. We managed, and I was helping my father. We got to the top of a hillock when we still heard the shooting. It was dark by that time." My question is: Can you remember any more details that could help the Trial Chamber, together with the statements of other eye-witnesses, which locations that was, and whether it's the same event that you are talking about? Do you have any more details to provide?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: The only detail I can give you about that is that there was a mass of people, really a lot of people - I can't tell how many; I don't want to speculate - at the time when the shooting started from all sides. That something I have flashbacks about to this day. When you see people being shot, when a bullet grazes your face, burning your skin without actually hitting you, and when you manage to get away unscathed and get to the top of that hillock I mentioned in the statement, and when we were still alive at nightfall, and when we realised that we had been ambushed, and when your soldiers got there -- I'll tell you one detail I hadn't mentioned many times because it's shocking, and when from that distance someone saying, "Take your underpants off. Fuck your balija mother," that's the detail that tells me it was an ambush and many, many, people got there -- many, many people got killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't receive interpretation at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you in shock and that's why you don't want to speculate about the number? You don't want to give a number that's lower or higher than the actual number; is that why you did not tell us the exact number of people?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I can only say it was a mass of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, since you can't determine how many, I would like to read to you from one statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab number 5, D268. We will not say the name of the person who gave this statement, but we'll quote from the last paragraph, the second half of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So I'm not going to mention name. This person told us later that during the withdrawal of 285th and 282nd Brigades, sometime around 1000 hours --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have that page on the screen anymore.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Tolimir be asked to repeat this passage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters had some difficulties to follow because the relevant page disappeared from the screen at that moment. Please repeat the last part of your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "Sometime around 1000 hours on the same day, a Chetnik paramilitary unit opened strong artillery fire on other -- on the remaining brigades and civilian population that happened to be in Buljim, where," according to his statement, "around 1.000 soldiers and civilians were killed. The shelling was from anti-aircraft weapons, Pragas, zoljas, and RPGs." Based on this passage from this eye-witness, can you determine whether it was the same incident, whether it indeed happened that way, the horrible way that he describes?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I'm not interested in the details provided by others. I'm here to tell you about what I personally experienced and saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I only wanted to refresh your memory, because you didn't say anything about that, and to try to determine the location. Do you know where that happened and the name of that location so the Trial Chamber can have an idea where the column was attacked?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I think Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that Pobudjanska Kamenica, or some other Kamenica, maybe the Zvornik Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, since you said that you fell asleep on that spot and you couldn't find your father and brother, you found them only later, can you tell us perhaps whether they told you how this ambush had occurred, along with the other circumstances that you were unable to describe in your statement?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There is no sound from the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please stop for a moment. We didn't hear the answer of the witness. It was not heard and not interpreted and not recorded. I would kindly ask the witness to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Have you spoken to your brother and father at all about how it had come about that you were separated while you fell asleep and how come they left you there? Have you ever discussed it with them?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: How can you speak to a father whose whereabouts I never learned? He was never identified, even, and I didn't speak about it to my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at page 3 of your statement, where you say: "After a while --" Page 3. That's the same statement of this witness, page 3, first paragraph. "After some time --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, first you said page 3 of your statement. Now you say statement of this witness. Are you now referring to D268?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D319. I stressed page 3. It's page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "After a while, things were quiet again. I found my brother, and then I fell asleep again. When I woke up, it was already in daytime. I couldn't find my brother or father. There were about 15 dead bodies lying there, in civilian clothes, some of them had their throats cut and some of the bodies were cut into two or in fragments, blasted to fragments. From the stench and the sight, I started throwing up. I was terrified and ran away." Tell me, is it a different location now? Did you run away to that hillock, fell asleep, and then woke up in a different place where you saw this? Can you tell us something more about this location?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything about this in particular. Nothing new. I stand by what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We are still on D319, paragraph 2 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which is under seal and should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Serbian it's page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "Sometime later I came across another group of people, and we continued along the track made by those who had passed ahead of us. There I found my father and brother again. We heard the Serbs calling for us to surrender on their megaphones." At this location, did you find out from your brother or father how come that you kept falling asleep and then became reunited with them when such horrible things were going on?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: After leaving Srebrenica, when you came to Dubrava, and later, did you discuss the events in Srebrenica with your brother, and did he tell what had happened on the 13th of July around 1.30 p.m. while you were sleeping and they had already left and you were unable to find them?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No, I don't like to talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, let us look at tab 2, statement 5933. Page 3 in Serbian, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The number is P933.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, this statement is not under seal, but it's probably, out of an abundance of caution, better to not broadcast it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And should not be broadcast. Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I am quoting from paragraph 3, that's page 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Aleksandar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Quoting from what your brother said: "After that incident, around 0400 hours, from a distance of about 500 metres, Serbs called us on their megaphones to surrender. We lingered for a while, and then the young man who had opened fire on those men who were supposedly Serbs gave me a rifle and told me and another young man to go up to the hill and check if there were Serbs around. Suddenly, we were told to stop and someone asked us where we were headed. We told them we were from Srebrenica, and they replied they were members from a mountain battalion of the Bosnian army. When we approached them, I recognised one man from this battalion. Actually, he was a distant cousin of mine," I won't read out the name, "I don't know his last name. He was a messenger this battalion, and I told him about the shooting incident. And then this man," whose name I'm not going to read out, "confirmed that the three men were from their -- his unit and told us to go back and inform the others about this." Does your cousin say here, in line 6, those who were supposedly Serbs; does it mean that he doubted they were Serbs? And later, in lines 9 and 10, we see that he found those were actually members of a mountain battalion who was supposed to protect you. Can you tell us, is it possible that at this location described by your cousin you were shot at by a unit of that mountain battalion holding themselves out to be Serbs, and they even told you to withdraw?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Only if that mountain battalion was driving an UNPROFOR APC and wearing UNPROFOR uniforms and calling us balija mother fuckers, only in that case it could be true. But I doubt it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I would like to clarify one matter. The statement the witness could see and read, and you have quoted from, Mr. Tolimir, is this statement from your brother or your cousin?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm asking the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that this is my brother's statement. I never saw it before. He personally did not tell me anything about this statement either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm asking you that because Mr. Tolimir used the term "your cousin," but at the beginning, "your brother." Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, and there seems to be -- I mean, to be fair to the witness, the passage that General Tolimir read out is referring to a time when this witness was not with his brother, as can be seen from paragraph 5, on page 3 of the English version, where he says that he later joined -- found his brother and joined him. And the witness was seemingly answering the question with an understanding that this incident that the brother describes in the paragraph that General Tolimir read is, in fact, an event that took place later when he was present and heard the calls to surrender. So we're talking about two different things, and I think it's confusing the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on, but bear that in mind if that is correct what Ms. Hasan said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In my previous questions I asked the witness whether it was possible that they were shot at by soldiers from the Brcko Battalion. He said, "No." Later, I read a part of his brother's statement where it says that they were shot at by the Brcko Mountain Battalion. Let's look at P933, second page, second paragraph, or the paragraph before the one that we have just read.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Where it says, and I quote -- I'm quoting from paragraph 3 of the witness's brother's statement, where it says: "A young man in my group --" I apologise. I didn't say that that document was under tab 2. And I repeat my quote: "A young man in my group, I don't know his name, told me to lie down. He had a machine-gun and wanted to fire upon those three men who he said were Chetniks. He opened fire, he killed the two in uniform and hit the third one with a first aid kit in the knee. He remained lying in the grass next to a creek. He asked for help. He said that he was a Muslim but nobody believed him. We left him in the area." And later on, I would like to say that in the third paragraph of your brother's statement we saw that your cousin told your brother that those soldiers were from the Mountain Battalion of the Bosnian Army. That's what he stated in line 6, paragraph 3. I'm asking you this: Does it transpire from this that the soldier who had an automatic rifle and who said to your brother to lie down opened fire and killed the Bosnian army soldier, having mistaken him for a Serb? Is that what it says in your brother's statement?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know, and I'm not interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I know that you're not interested in this; however, please, did people open fire at each other? Did they kill each other? And did you see and hear that while you were moving through the forest before you surrendered?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: People went mad. I saw a case when a man through a grenade and killed a man in his vicinity, but that was not happening on a large-scale basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Where were you when things were happening as described by your brother in his statement in passages 2 and 3, where he says that Muslims were the ones who were killing BiH Army soldiers?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I did not have a measuring tape. I could not know where I was, at what distance. I don't know where he was, what he was doing. I told you that I lost him on two or three occasions, and I don't know what he saw, what he did. If you have questions for me about what I saw, I'm here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, I do have a question for you. Let's go to paragraph 4 in your brother's statement, where it says: "When I returned to the young man, he had the automatic rifle and I told him that our soldiers were in the area and I gave the rifle back to him. He told us that we could not join them as we did not have any weapons." My question: Does it transpire from this part of your brother's statement that he had warned the soldier who had given him the rifle that he was actually killing "our own men," and returned the rifle to him? Did -- would you agree that your brother saw that this man in his group was killing BiH Army soldiers?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's been a line of questions now about passages from his brother's statement, when clearly the witness was not present. If it's simply to confirm what the document said, respectively, I submit, there's not much value in doing so, in just reading out passages and seeing whether the witness is confirming what the brother has said in this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is really a question whether this kind of question is helping to find out the truth, that's true, especially because P933 is already in evidence. On the other hand, Mr. Tolimir is entitled to put these parts of this statement to the witness if he is able to confirm the content or not, and he receives the answers the witness could give him. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In order to arrive at the absolute truth, I will put another question to this witness. In the last part of this fourth paragraph, your brother says: "He told us that we could not join them as we did not have any weapons." My question is this: Did the BiH Army soldiers have a special mission or a special task, given the fact that they did not allow those without weapons to join them? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did they need men with weapons only because they had been given the task to kill people, in view of the fact that civilians were an integral part of the column?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? Your microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since you were deployed as civilians with the Mountain Battalion, how come that all of a sudden they told people that they could not allow civilians without weapons to join them, although their task was to protect civilians? Was that because their task was to kill people and that's why they only needed men with weapons? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: First of all, I was not deployed anywhere with any unit. And as for who killed whom, we shouldn't be the judge of that. We have the Judges to be the judge of that. And if you are trying to put to me that I saw members of the Mountain Battalion in Buljim and if you are mixing up my words with the words of my brother, I respectfully don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm not mixing things up. I'm just quoting from your statement where you said that you were lined up by BiH Army officers, that you were lined up by them to form a column. You said that on page 1 of your statement, D319, line 2 and 3. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is your question in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: Why were you mixed up with the military column? Why did Bosnian army civilians deploy you with a military column and you were civilians?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: There was no military column. Let me repeat: Buljim and Kamenica and Sandici, where we were, are not one and the same thing. If there were some attempts to organise a column in Buljim and Jaglic [phoen], and that column consisted of civilians - I would like to emphasize that - I don't see what kind of a military column are you talking about. Who was it who made up a military column? I don't see much point in your question. What you are implying? What you are trying to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated, in lines 8 and 9, There were about fifty armed soldiers among us. This means that you were mixed up with the soldiers of the Mountain Battalion; am I right or not?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: There were fifty armed soldiers in Buljim, but that does not mean that those soldiers walked with any of the groups or with me, personally, from then on. I only stated that I had seen them in Buljim and never again after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I have just quoted from a statement, and I don't want to mention the name of the soldier who provided the statement. In that statement, the soldier says, and this statement is D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Tolimir repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please repeat the number again of this statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 5, D268. Paragraph 3. We will not mention any names. In paragraph 3 of this statement, line 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is the third line from the bottom, where it says: "On that occasion, the 285th Brigade set out first, and it was followed by the 282nd. And his father and his brother were with the latter brigade, and I don't know about -- anything about their fate from then on. Enver told us further on that when the 285th and the 282nd Brigades ..." and so on and so forth. My question is this: Do other witnesses speak about the brigades and where they were deployed, were they were mixed up? Can you conclude that from this statement?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't want to interpret other peoples' statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, let's look at tab 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to clarify if we have reason to redact page 40, line 19, because there was a name mentioned. I think we should. I see agreement by the parties. We will do that. And please wait for the next document, and then put the next question to the witness. Tab 9 is the document D180.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This document is not under seal and I don't see the basis for the redaction. Perhaps we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We go, for a short time, into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir. Ms. Hasan, I see you on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, Mr. President. I think we have to go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And now we see in front of us: "Handbook on the Law of War for Armed Forces." This was published by the International Red Cross. It brings The Hague and the Geneva Conventions and how they regulate the rules of war. You said that you were not a military analyst, but let's look at pages 3 and 5, paragraph 56, in the Serbian and English respectively. Now we can see paragraph 56. Can it be zoomed in. It's the first paragraph from the top where it says: "A military target remains a military target even if civilian persons are in it. The civilian persons within such a target or object or its immediate surroundings share the danger to which it is exposed." My question to you is this: If civilians are mixed up with a military column or in its vicinity, would you say that they also become a military target? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If I may, before the witness answers this question, the witness was 16 years old at the time. He's not a legal expert nor is he a military analyst, as he's already said. I don't see where this question is going, and I don't think this is an appropriate witness to put that kind of a question to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Even if I agree, I would say the witness could provide us with exactly such an answer. Sir, are you able to answer this question of Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, I will answer your question. In no case was this a legitimate military target. My answer is this: There were no legitimate military targets because there was nobody there but civilians. If we're talking about the column as it was up to Sandici, under no definition could that be considered a legitimate military target.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Bearing in mind what the Prosecutor said and bearing in mind how old you were, that's why I quoted this. You said you were not a military expert, but those military officers who mixed you up with a column should have been aware of the rules of war. Would you agree with that, yes or no, those who lined you up at Buljim and mixed you up with the military column, were they supposed to know what they were doing in accordance with the military rules and laws?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not sure if this is a correct representation of what the witness told us about the soldiers and the composition of the column where he was in. Please be careful in phrasing your questions. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions about this. I know that the witness was young and he was not in a position to know anything about that, but there were soldiers there and they should have known. In any way, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, please, could you tell us whether you have recently heard of a problem or a projection of a film about Srebrenica in Sweden and Muslims have protested against that. I don't know where you currently live; that's why I am asking you.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know that on television in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in the Republika Srpska there was a programme featuring eye-witnesses of the breakthrough and how the massacre happened. Do you know who Meholjic is? He was one of the eye-witnesses.

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: Meholjic does ring a bell, but I did not see the programme and I did not hear those statements. I would love to hear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, we will now look at the statement of Mr. Meholjic. It's under tab 3. It's D277. The title of the document is: "5.000 Muslim Heads in Exchange for a Military Intervention." That's an interview with Hakija Meholjic, president of War Presidency of Srebrenica, given to a Bosnian newspaper called "Dani." I will just quote from the introduction: "In your accusations against the state leadership, and particularly against President Izetbegovic, saying they are partly to blame for the tragedy in Srebrenica, the departure of the Srebrenica delegation to Sarajevo in September 1993 for talks about the fate of this enclave is an inevitable subject." And then the interviewer asks: "So you rejected Izetbegovic's offer?" And Meholjic answers: "We rejected it without any discussion. Then he said: 'You know, I was offered by Clinton in April 1993 (after the fall of Cerska and Konjevic Polje) that the Chetnik forces should enter Srebrenica, carry out a slaughter of 5.000 Muslims, and then there will be a military intervention.'" My question to you is: Have you ever heard anything about this?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we turn the page now to look at page 2, where the interviewer asks Mr. Meholjic the following question: "Even after the fall of Srebrenica in 1995, you had occasion to address President Izetbegovic?" Meholjic answers: "At that time, I requested that a state commission be established to inquiry into the responsibility of the international community, the responsibility of the president, the General Staff, the 2nd Corps, and our own responsibility ... people are missing ... and he," meaning President Izetbegovic, "asked me: 'And what would that give me?'" Do you know that this topic was on the table in 1993, in 1994, in 1995, even after the fall of Srebrenica and the tragedy in Srebrenica, and that it's still topical in the public opinion of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: In 1993 to 1995, my only thoughts were about finding some food to survive. The rest is rubbish. I didn't care what was going on around. I know only what happened to me. I don't care about what Hakija said or what Clinton said. I know that my family and many other people were killed. There was 67 men in my village before the war, and now we are four men. They were all killed. What Hakija and all these people are saying, I don't care, and I couldn't have heard it, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I have to stop you. The first reason is he was really a boy at that time, 1993; he was 14 years old. I think you should focus on what you can gain from him and which knowledge he has from his point of view. We must have our second break now. I would like to ask you how much time you will need for the remainder of your cross-examination, have you any idea?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The witness said that he would like to hear what Meholjic said, so I showed him. And I have one minute of video footage to show him what Meholjic said, and after that I will move to my final questions. Thank you. I will need perhaps 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We must have, on technical reasons, our second break now. But before we break, I have to discuss one matter in private session. We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, we must have now our second break. We will resume 5 minutes before 2.00. And I hope very much that we are able to finish the examination of this witness during the next session and that we are able to discuss procedural matters about the further planning of this case. We adjourn and resume 5 minutes before 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We turn into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we now see in e-court 1D952, a clip from a documentary about Srebrenica shown on Dutch television. 03:00 to 03:30, just 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you able to give us an idea when this was broadcast, by which Dutch television channel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This has been shown more than once. This statement of Meholjic is -- can be found in a hundred different places. References were made to it during the war and after the war. But we'll find exactly the provenance and we'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question for the witness: You heard what Meholjic stated as an eye-witness participant in the events, who has gone even a longer way than you. You heard what your brother said about the involvement of the soldiers of the Mountain Battalion in the killing of civilians in the column. So can you tell us, as an eye-witness, anything about how the soldiers of the Mountain Battalion treated the civilians who were together with you in the column? And do you know if they were participating in putting into practice this idea of President Clinton of the USA?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I can only comment on what Meholjic said. That would be the same as if someone told me to kill a certain number of Serbs. Nobody can make me, force me, do something that I am not willing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for the answer. Let us now move to the last part of your statement, on page 4, paragraph 4. It's tab 1, 06516, already admitted as D319. I forgot to say this statement has not been admitted. I should like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The statement from tab 2 which is -- in fact, Aleksandar tells me that it has been admitted already. Thank you, Aleksandar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's now P933 under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the meantime, you were able to read your own statement, paragraph 4. I quote: "Then a bus full of women arrived from that direction, as well as a car."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you wait, please, until we have it on the screen. You were referring to page 4, paragraph 4. Are you referring to the B/C/S version or to the English?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both English and B/C/S, page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now it is on the screen. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR.  TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I quote: "The second time I went to get water --" No, sorry, that's the wrong paragraph. Paragraph 4. "Then a bus full of women arrived from the same direction as the car and stopped next to the fountain. A driver came out of the car to get water. I dropped the jerrycans, sneaked onto the bus, and hid between the seats. I put some bags on top of myself." My question is: How are you able to get onto the bus when the driver did not come out nor did the soldiers who were guarding the civilians? How could you get in unnoticed and without permission when you were getting water for the driver of the car that was escorting the bus?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: This is obviously a mistake in the recording. I never said that the driver got out of the car. Every time I spoke about it, I said explicitly the driver of the bus got out and crossed the road to speak to the soldiers who were standing there. This must be a mistake in the statement by the person who recorded it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I think we can clarify the situation. In the English translation, I quote: "The driver came out of the bus to collect water." Which is exactly the same as the witness just said. In the -- when Mr. Tolimir read this part into the transcript, it was interpreted as "came out of the car," which is not the English version. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the two versions differ in this passage. The Serbian version says "automobile," not "bus." If you look at the relevant paragraph, line 2, you will see the word is "automobile." It is written in the same way or in a similar way as in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You are absolutely right, but now we have received the clarification from the witness. He is referring to the driver of the bus. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Sir, you saw where the problem is. It must be a wrong translation. I'm asking you: Were there any soldiers guarding the civilians on that bus in addition to that car that was guarding the bus?

utterances.speaker: PW-014
utterances.text: I never saw those soldiers. I saw the driver coming out of the bus. I didn't see any soldiers on the bus.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to thank the witness for having participated in these proceedings. I wish him all the best. I wish for all of his wishes to come true. God be with him. The Defence has no further questions for this witness. This brings our cross-examination to an end. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Hasan, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No re-examination, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir, you will be pleased to hear that this concludes your examination here in this trial. The Chamber would like to thank you that you were able to provide us with your recollection of the relevant events. The Chamber, like Mr. Tolimir, wishes you the best for your future, and now you are free to return to your normal activities. Thank you very much again that you were able to communicate with us via videolink today. I would like to ask the Registrar who is present there if everything is prepared to conclude the video conference.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [via videolink] [Microphone not activated] Your Honours, I hereby confirm that we are ready to conclude. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am very sorry, but we couldn't hear the answer because, I think, this is only in the B/C/S channel. I think this brings everything to an end.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank the Trial Chamber for inviting me to provide my testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The videolink is concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, last week we heard from Mr. Gajic that he will be able to provide us, one week after the conclusion of the testimony of Mr. Butler, with the estimate and your planning for the further trial, for your Defence case, how much time you will need, and what are your intentions. We would be very glad if we could receive now some more information about your plans. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, our estimate is that we have a lot of time and we believe that we will be able to start presenting the Defence case after the winter recess. We still have a lot of material to review, some of it I have to receive in Belgrade after the end of the Prosecution case. Our experts still have a lot of work to do. Unfortunately, Mr. Butler testified very recently and it will take some time to review his testimony. However, we will do our best to be ready as soon as the winter recess is over. As for the 65 ter list of exhibits that we want to use during the Defence case, we would like to submit that on the eve of the winter recess so as to enable everybody to prepare adequate translations during the winter break. As for the Defence case, don't hold me to my estimate because we still have to establish the number of witnesses, but we believe that we will need about a month to present our case if we continue working four days a week.
