And I would kindly ask both the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution to take this as a rather realistic estimate, more to the detriment of the Defence than anything else, because there is really a lot of material that we have to review in the meantime. We have had some problems with translations. Mr. Tolimir does not speak English. The transcript is voluminous, which poses an additional difficulty. I don't know whether you believe me when I say that all of our team members are engaged in translation. Obviously, we need some time to translate our expert witnesses' reports, and we will do our best to provide all those translation before the end of the winter recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Gajic, that the whole Defence case will last one month. Is that your rough estimation for the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Unless we are not given enough time for preparations, a month. What we can announce already now, that in addition to the witnesses we will also submit a request to bar -- to tender some of the exhibits from bar table, and this, I believe, will facilitate the entire Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, I am quite astonished to hear that you are requesting a four-month break for preparation of the Defence case. This is a rather long period. If you compare that with other cases in this Tribunal, this is really a rather long time. Does the Prosecution have something to submit in that respect? Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, good afternoon. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I think I will largely put that ball back in your court. It is a long time. The general is mostly representing himself and there is a lot of material, and I'm happy to hear that it's only a one-month Defence case. But having said that, I would, again, rely on the judgement of the Trial Chamber to do the best thing on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I hate to object. You said four months, but that also includes the winter recess, which starts in mid-December and ends around mid-January, and we have counted that in. I could have also told you that we can start on the last day before the recess. The recess will be a working time for us, unlike some other Defence teams which had two Defence counsel, Case Managers, and investigators. I have to say that this is the smallest Defence team in the history of the Tribunal. There is a lot of work, a lot of translation work; that is why I appeal to you for your understanding. During that time, this legal advisor will have to travel thousands of kilometres, not only between Belgrade and The Hague but also to some other destinations where we will have to interview some potential witnesses and obtain certain documents. Unfortunately, things take time. When we submit requests for documentation, it also takes time for those documents to be located and to be sent. And I believe that my learned friends from the Prosecution will understand when I say that when they receive a document, they first have to check what of those things are relevant, what not. Some of those documents are already ready for me to pick up. I have to go personally to those locations and to pick up the documentation, but I don't know what I will find there. Also, we have received some materials pursuant to Rule 68 from the Prosecutor only recently. We have to review those. We have not had time to do that. There are some other disclosure as well. Yesterday, or the day before yesterday, you had an occasion to hear how many documents are there in the Pecanac collection. All those are factors that I believe have to be borne in mind when considering the time required by the Defence to prepare. Also, our experts have a lot of things to do. During the trial, I have slept four hours a night, but I can't expect the same from our experts and other individuals who are going to be involved in the preparations for the Defence case. Obviously, we would like to prepare our case so that everything runs smoothly without any glitches or delays. Obviously, if things are well prepared, that can be done and we will be able to present all of our Defence case within the scope of one month. One more thing we have had in mind: When bringing our witnesses in, we don't want to bring those witnesses who will repeat things that already are on file. We want to provide the Trial Chamber with some new information which may be of a very high relevance for this Trial Chamber's decision. On my internal list, I already have somebody who may be called to provide an adequate testimony, but first I have to check whether this will indeed be of help to the Trial Chamber or whether this will be a repetition of things that are already known. We don't want to go over the same grounds again. We would like to provide the Trial Chamber with new things, something that they have not heard before. We want our experts to provide proper and good analysis. Unfortunately, all that takes time, and we believe that the time-span which brings us to the end of the winter recess is an adequate period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this. Before I give the floor, Mr. McCloskey, I would like to confirm that Mr. Gajic was not sleeping enough during the trial. One night we received at 4.00 in the morning and 16 minutes an e-mail from Mr. Gajic, which I read only in the morning, not during night-time. This is just a confirmation of what he just said. Thank you for your information about your proposed work. The Chamber will take that into account, of course. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It may be helpful if we can get an estimate on when the experts will be done with their reports, because if there are experts, like a military expert, as suggested by Mr. Gajic, and if they are Serbian, it is, of course, important for us all to have an English translation. And if it's a lengthy Butler-type report, that will, of course, take some time for CLSS. And I don't -- a matter of this import, we really will need an English translation prior to cross-examination. So that's just one logistical detail to bear in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber will consider the submissions by the parties and the request of the Defence. We will come back to the parties next week before the close of the Prosecution case. Mr. Gajic, you have the floor again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to Mr. McCloskey's question I would like to answer by saying that when we requested this period of time to prepare for our Defence case, we have had in mind this concern of his. Obviously, we would not want to call the witness without giving the Trial Chamber an opportunity to review the material that such a witness will be discussed in the courtroom. I will do my best to chase our experts and ask them to finish as soon as possible, but there are a lot of materials. They will have a lot of work. I repeat, I will try to concentrate on only the most important and relevant things. Please rest assured that the time-period that we have requested is only the minimum time-period that we really need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, again. I think we have now everything on the record, and we will take it into our consideration. One last matter I just want to raise. On the 7th of July, last year, 2010, we heard Witness Zlatan Celanovic, and during cross-examination, Mr. Tolimir, you used parts of the book "Chronicles of our Graveyard." The same day, the Chamber invited the parties to try to find an agreement which parts of this book should be tendered and received into evidence because the translation of the whole book would be a heavy burden for the Translation Unit. Therefore, I would kindly ask you next week to provide us with your common understanding about the parts of this book which should be translated. There is no translation yet of the whole book. Therefore, in order to finalise these things before the close of the Prosecution case, we would be glad if we could receive such a submission next would, too. Thank you very much. This concludes the hearing of today. We will resume on Monday, 2.15, in this courtroom. We adjourn for the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of September, 2011, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.46 p.m.,
